# CharterMesh

CharterMesh is a provider-neutral organization-as-code control plane for AI
work.

When asked to apply this repository to another project, read BOOTSTRAP.md and
use its inspect -> plan -> exact human approval -> apply -> verify protocol.
With only the GitHub URL, the package-ready entry point is
`npx --yes github:jade-blanco/chartermesh` after package-download approval.
Tool execution is governed by OrgSpec allowlists, relative workspace roots,
exact-call human approvals, evidence hashes, and bounded iterations.
Any local executable can connect through the shell-free command-process JSON
contract; its approved executable digest is pinned and it runs from a dedicated
cwd. Unknown model cost follows the user's OrgSpec policy and is never silently
zero. Allowlisted audit export and DB+artifact backup/restore remain local.
Runtime JSON is schema-validated before inference. Model calls are recorded
before start and share durable CLI/dashboard/signal cancellation. Work lists
support cursors and archive, audit export streams, outbox delivery retries and
dead-letters, and optional local schedules are disabled by default and start
zero models on an empty queue.
Decision Packet v1alpha2 separately binds exact artifact bytes/media type and
the canonical producer-report sidecar. Producer-reported checks remain
claimed, including in experimental runtime_compiled mode. Human decision
surfaces must show the exact bounded artifact preview as well as the packet;
the projection is not a substitute for the deliverable. SQLite schema v12
stores report JSON, hash, and byte size. runtime_compiled is currently a
BuiltInManagedRunner API option, not a CLI/runtime.json setting.
Approved bootstrap plans also install four provider-neutral Apache-2.0 Agent
Skills. External MCP servers remain uninstalled and disabled. Optional
SearXNG web.search requires a reviewed HTTPS/loopback endpoint, a tool-calling
engine, an OrgSpec allowlist entry, and exact per-query human approval.

The evaluate-decision-review command is dry by default. Its live mode requires
the exact plan hash and an attested Codex executable/model binding for 20
stateless calls over the fixed ten-case raw/decision_review suite. The plan
also binds the exact local harness-source digest and the live runner compares
the complete regenerated plan before starting. Fatal identity, executable, or
unsettled-process failures stop the study. The result is descriptive proxy
regression evidence only, never human, causal, statistical, approval, or
autonomy evidence.
Quota/rate capacity and authentication boundaries pause this benchmark after
the child settles, without scoring the attempted call. An operator signal is
resumable only between calls; Ctrl+C during an active model call leaves an
unknown outcome and fails closed. Each invocation is durably marked before
launch, and running, failed, active, or unknown attempts are never retried
automatically. A clean paused checkpoint lives only under
`.chartermesh/evaluations/<benchmarkId>/checkpoint.json`; the final report
alone is written to exports. Resume is a dry
`--resume --account-context same|changed|unknown` plan followed by a fresh
exact `RESUME_PLAN_HASH` approval. The completed prefix is immutable and the
model, executable/hash, limits, suite, protocols, and source digest must still
match. No account/email/auth-path/credential fingerprint is stored; context is
operator-declared and unverified. Every resume creates a new segment and
confounds a strict uninterrupted reviewer-benefit claim; changed or unknown
also discloses account-continuity uncertainty. Source changes invalidate old
plan hashes.
Each resumed segment binds its source checkpoint, prior segment chain, attempt
count, and approval hash; an exclusive used-approval receipt is written before
the next model process. Dead-owner stale-lock recovery is allowed only for the
exact clean paused state. State-path symlink/junction components are rejected.
These are single-user local hash controls, not signatures or protection from a
malicious local writer or whole-directory rollback.
